chunks.title: The AI assistant › What the assistant does
chunks.text:
The Axoview AI button (bottom right, signed-in users) opens a chat. Ask how to do
something in Axoview and it answers from this manual, citing the sections it
used. Ask about your diagram and it can suggest changes as a checklist. It never
edits your diagram: you make every change yourself.

chunks.title: The AI assistant › Getting suggestions for your diagram
chunks.text:
Tick Include this page before sending. The assistant then sees the open
page's item names, icons, connections, rectangles and text, and can suggest
steps such as "Connect Web server to Database" or "Group API and Worker in a
rectangle called Private subnet". Each suggestion is checked against your page:
one that refers to something that is not there is shown as not applicable, with
the reason. Tick suggestions off as you make them.

Without Include this page, nothing from your diagram is sent.

chunks.title: The AI assistant › What is sent and kept
chunks.text:
- Your message, and the page summary when you include it, are sent to Amazon
  Nova through Amazon Bedrock and checked by a content-safety guardrail.
- The conversation (your messages and the replies) is kept for 30 days. The page
  summary is used for that one reply and is not stored.
- Prompts and replies are never written to the service logs.

chunks.title: The AI assistant › Limits
chunks.text:
Each account has a daily number of AI requests (20 unless your site sets
another); the count resets at midnight UTC. Messages are up to 2,000 characters.
When the limit is reached the assistant says so until the next day.

chunks.title: The AI assistant › Using this manual from other AI tools
chunks.text:
The manual is public, so any AI tool can read it:

- As files: /llms.txt on the Axoview site lists every page, and
  /llms-full.txt holds the whole manual as one text file. Each page is also at
  /docs/manual/<page>.md.
- Over MCP: where the site offers it, add https://<your Axoview site>/api/mcp
  as a remote MCP server in Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini CLI or another MCP client. It
  needs no sign-in and has two read-only tools: search_manual finds the
  sections that answer a question, and get_manual_section returns one section.

Neither gives access to your diagrams or your account: only this manual.

chunks.title: Working with the canvas › Zooming
chunks.text:
Scroll the mouse wheel to zoom. By default the zoom moves toward the cursor; turn
off Zoom to Cursor in Settings → Canvas to zoom around the centre instead.
The zoom controls (bottom right) have Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit to
screen. Keep labels readable keeps label text a readable size when you
zoom far out.

chunks.title: Working with the canvas › Panning (moving around)
chunks.text:
- Hold the right mouse button and drag, or drag with the middle button.
- The arrow keys nudge the canvas.
- The Pan tool (hotkey M) makes a left-drag pan. A right-click without
  dragging toggles pan mode; a left-click returns to select.

chunks.title: Working with the canvas › Rotating the isometric view
chunks.text:
- Q turns the floor 15° counter-clockwise and E 15° clockwise; with
  Shift they jump to the next quarter turn.
- Alt + drag orbits freely; hold Shift while orbiting to snap to 15°.
- The rotation controls show the current angle. Set as page default makes
  this page open at that angle for everyone; Unpin page default returns it to
  0°. Both are one undo step.

Rotation is only available in the isometric view.

chunks.title: Working with the canvas › Switching between 2D and isometric
chunks.text:
The tool menu has Switch to 2D view and Switch to isometric view. The
diagram is the same; only the projection changes.

chunks.title: Working with the canvas › Selecting items
chunks.text:
- Click an item to select it; click empty canvas to clear the selection.
- Ctrl/Cmd + click adds or removes an item from the selection.
- Drag on empty canvas, or use the Lasso select tool (L), to draw a
  selection box. Freehand lasso (F) selects everything inside a shape
  you draw.
- Ctrl+A selects every visible, unlocked item on the page.
- Once several items are selected, drag inside the selection to move them
  together.
- The Select tool (S) returns to normal selection.

chunks.title: Working with the canvas › The context menu
chunks.text:
Right-click without dragging (long-press on touch) to open the context menu: the
item menu over an item, the canvas menu over empty space. It has Details…,
Rename, Add/edit note, Add label, Cut, Copy, Paste,
Duplicate, stacking order, Assign to layer, grid and collision options
and Delete.

chunks.title: Working with the canvas › Undo and redo
chunks.text:
Ctrl+Z undoes; Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes (Cmd on Mac). The tool
menu also has Undo and Redo buttons. Deleting, cutting, pasting and
changing a page's default angle can all be undone.

chunks.title: Connectors › Connecting two items
chunks.text:
Press C or click Connector in the tool menu. Then, in the default click
mode, click the first item (or a point on the canvas) and then the second item.
In drag mode, drag from the first item to the second. Esc cancels.

Choose the mode in Settings → Connector Settings → Connection Creation
Mode: Click Mode (Recommended) or Drag Mode. The tool menu also shows
Click / Drag while the connector tool is active.

chunks.title: Connectors › Rerouting a connector
chunks.text:
Select the connector, then click a point on its line and drag: this adds a
waypoint or moves an existing one. Alt + click a waypoint removes it (the
connector does not need to be selected); the two ends stay attached.

chunks.title: Connectors › Attaching a loose end
chunks.text:
If a connector end is not attached to an item, drag that end onto the item you
want it connected to.

chunks.title: Connectors › Naming a connector and adding labels
chunks.text:
Double-click a connector (or Details…) to open its panel:

- Name is the connector's main text (for example "HTTPS" or "writes to").
- Labels → Add label adds extra text along the line. Drag a label on
  the canvas to move it along the connector; use the top bar for its text size
  and colour. On double lines, choose Line 1 or Line 2.
- Notes holds longer text that is not drawn.

chunks.title: Connectors › Connector colour and line style
chunks.text:
Select a connector and use the top bar:

- Connection color sets its colour.
- Line options → Line style (solid, dotted, dashed), Line type
  (single, double, double with circle), Width and Show arrow.

With the connector tool active and nothing selected, the same controls set the
colour and line style of the next connector you draw.

chunks.title: Connectors › Deleting a connector
chunks.text:
Click the connector's line to select it, then press Delete (Backspace on
Mac) or choose Delete in its context menu. The items it joined stay where
they are. Ctrl+Z brings the connector back.

chunks.title: Getting started › What Axoview is
chunks.text:
Axoview is a diagram editor for isometric (3D-looking) and flat 2D diagrams of
cloud, network and software architecture. It ships with general icons and AWS,
Google Cloud, Azure and Kubernetes icon packs. You draw by placing items (icons),
joining them with connectors, and grouping them with rectangles, text boxes and
labels.

chunks.title: Getting started › Signing in
chunks.text:
On the hosted Axoview site the editor opens at /app and asks you to sign in
first. Sign in with your Axoview account, or with Google when the sign-in page
offers it. Your diagrams are then kept on the server under your account, so they
are there the next time you sign in from any browser.

To sign out, open the account menu (your user name, top right) and choose
Sign out.

chunks.title: Getting started › The Diagrams panel
chunks.text:
The left dock holds four panels: File explorer (Diagrams), Elements,
Layers and Settings. The Diagrams panel lists your diagrams under
This server. Its toolbar has New diagram, New folder, Import,
Export project, Refresh and Collapse all.

- Click a diagram to open it.
- Right-click a diagram for Open, Rename, Duplicate, Copy share
  link, Export as image…, Export as JSON and Delete.
- Right-click a folder for New diagram, New folder, Rename,
  Export folder… and Delete. Deleting a folder also deletes the
  diagrams inside it; Axoview asks first.

The Elements and Layers panels say "open or create a diagram first" until a
diagram is open.

chunks.title: Getting started › Creating a diagram
chunks.text:
Click New diagram in the Diagrams panel (or on the empty start screen). Give
it a name; you can rename it later from the page tabs (pencil, Rename
diagram) or with F2 when nothing is selected.

chunks.title: Getting started › Saving
chunks.text:
The status area at the top shows whether the open diagram is saved: Saved at
a time, Modified or Unsaved. Press Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on Mac) or use
Save to save it. Ctrl+O (Cmd+O) opens a diagram.

chunks.title: Getting started › Pages
chunks.text:
A diagram can have up to five pages, shown as tabs along the bottom of the
canvas. Each page is a separate drawing that shares the diagram's items list.

- Add page (the + after the tabs) adds one; at five pages the button says
  "Page limit reached (5)".
- The pencil on a tab renames it; the bin, Delete page, removes it.

chunks.title: Items, icons and labels › Adding an item
chunks.text:
Press N or click Add item in the tool menu to open the Elements
panel. Search for an icon (Search icons), then drag it onto the canvas or
click it and click where it should go. RECENTLY USED lists the icons you
placed most recently.

chunks.title: Items, icons and labels › Icon packs
chunks.text:
The core icon set is always loaded. AWS Icons, Google Cloud Icons,
Azure Icons and Kubernetes Icons are extra packs you can turn on or off
in Settings → Icon Pack Management. With Enable Lazy Loading on, a pack
loads the first time it is needed, which makes startup faster.

chunks.title: Items, icons and labels › Importing your own icons
chunks.text:
In the Elements panel, Import Icons adds PNG or SVG images as icons. Tick
Treat as isometric (3D view) for icons drawn in isometric perspective; untick
it for flat logos and UI elements. Generate icons with AI copies a prompt you
can paste into an image generator; replace "my object" with what you need and
import the PNG it makes.

chunks.title: Items, icons and labels › Name and label
chunks.text:
Every item has a Name and a Label (double-click the item, or
Details…, to see both under Metadata).

- The Name identifies the item; it is what the Layers panel lists.
- The Label is the text drawn on the canvas next to the item.

Renaming in the Layers panel does not change the label on the canvas. F2 or
Rename in the context menu renames the selected item inline.

chunks.title: Items, icons and labels › Showing, hiding and styling a label
chunks.text:
With an item selected, the top bar has Show label / Hide label, Label
size, Text color and Bold / italic / underline / strikethrough. With
several items selected, size and colour apply to all of them.

chunks.title: Items, icons and labels › Item details and notes
chunks.text:
Double-click an item (or choose Details…) to open its details panel, with
its name, label and Notes. Add/edit note in the context menu goes
straight to the notes. Notes are saved with the diagram.

chunks.title: Items, icons and labels › Changing an item's icon
chunks.text:
Select one item and use Change icon in the top bar. It changes one item at a
time.

chunks.title: Items, icons and labels › Linking an item
chunks.text:
Select an item and use Link in the top bar: Link to web takes a URL,
Link to diagram searches your other diagrams. Open linked diagram follows
the link.

chunks.title: Items, icons and labels › Deleting an item
chunks.text:
Select it and press Delete (Backspace on Mac), or choose Delete in the
context menu. Connectors attached to it are removed too. Ctrl+Z brings it
back.

chunks.title: Organising a diagram › Layers
chunks.text:
Open the Layers panel from the left dock. Add layer (+) creates a layer;
items are assigned with Assign to layer in the context menu, or by dragging
them in the panel. Items with no layer appear under Unassigned; drop items
there to unassign them.

Hide a layer to hide everything on it. Deleting a layer asks what to do with its
contents: Keep contents (they become unassigned and visible) or Delete
contents too.

chunks.title: Organising a diagram › Stacking order
chunks.text:
When items overlap, the context menu's Bring forward, Send backward,
Bring to front and Send to back change which is on top. Shortcuts:
Ctrl+] brings forward and Ctrl+[ sends backward; add Shift to jump
to the front or back.

chunks.title: Organising a diagram › Copy, cut, paste and duplicate
chunks.text:
Ctrl+C copies and Ctrl+X cuts the selection; Ctrl+V pastes at the
mouse position, offset so it does not land on top of the original. Connectors
between copied items are copied with them. Duplicate in the context menu
copies and pastes in one step.

chunks.title: Organising a diagram › Snap to grid and collision
chunks.text:
By default items snap to the grid and do not overlap. In the context menu,
Unsnap from grid lets an item sit between grid points, and Disable
collision lets it overlap others. Enable snap to grid / Disable snap to
grid in the canvas menu change the default for new items.

chunks.title: Settings and shortcuts › Settings
chunks.text:
Open Settings from the left dock.

- Language: the interface language.
- Zoom: Zoom to Cursor on or off.
- Connector Settings: Click Mode or Drag Mode for drawing connectors.
- Icon Pack Management: turn the AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and Kubernetes
  packs on or off, and Enable Lazy Loading.
- Labels: Expand Button Padding.

F1 (or Help in the zoom controls) opens Keyboard Shortcuts & Help
with the full list below.

chunks.title: Settings and shortcuts › Tool keys
chunks.text:
Tool keys work when you are not typing in a text field.

Key — Tool
S — Select
M — Pan
N — Add item (Elements panel)
R — Rectangle
C — Connector
T — Text
L — Lasso select
F — Freehand lasso
Esc — Cancel the current tool

chunks.title: Settings and shortcuts › Editing shortcuts
chunks.text:
Shortcut — Action
Ctrl+Z — Undo
Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z — Redo
Ctrl+X / Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V — Cut / copy / paste
Ctrl+A — Select all
Delete (Backspace on Mac) — Delete the selection
F2 — Rename the selected item, or the diagram
Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ — Bring forward / send backward (add Shift: to front / to back)
Ctrl+S / Ctrl+O — Save / open a diagram
Q / E — Rotate the view 15° (Shift: quarter turn)
F1 — Help

Use Cmd instead of Ctrl on a Mac.

chunks.title: Settings and shortcuts › Mouse and touch
chunks.text:
Action — Does
Click — Select an item; click empty canvas to deselect
Double-click — Open the item's details
Ctrl/Cmd + click — Add to or remove from the selection
Drag on empty canvas — Selection box
Right-drag or middle-drag — Pan
Right-click (long-press on touch) — Context menu
Scroll wheel — Zoom
Alt + drag — Orbit the view (Shift snaps to 15°)
Alt + click a waypoint — Remove the waypoint

chunks.title: Rectangles, text boxes and labels › Drawing a rectangle
chunks.text:
Press R or click Rectangle in the tool menu, then drag on the canvas.
Rectangles mark areas such as a VPC, a subnet, a region or a team boundary; they
sit under the items placed on them. Esc cancels.

chunks.title: Rectangles, text boxes and labels › Styling a rectangle
chunks.text:
Select it and use the top bar: Background color with Opacity, and
Border (Line style, Width, Border color). Give it a name in its
details panel; the name is what the Layers panel shows.

chunks.title: Rectangles, text boxes and labels › Adding a text box
chunks.text:
Press T or click Text in the tool menu, then click where the text should
go and type. Esc cancels. Text boxes hold paragraphs, so use them for
explanations and legends.

chunks.title: Rectangles, text boxes and labels › Formatting text in a text box
chunks.text:
While editing a text box, the top bar offers Text size, Line spacing,
Alignment (left, centre, right; top, middle, bottom), Text color, Bold
/ italic / underline / strikethrough, Bulleted list and Numbered list.
Select text and use Link selected text to add a link. Background color
and Border style the box itself; Fit to text in the context menu resizes
it to its content.

chunks.title: Rectangles, text boxes and labels › Floating labels
chunks.text:
A label is free text placed anywhere on the canvas, for example a title above a
group. Click Label in the tool menu and click to place it, or choose Add
label in the canvas context menu. Labels can have a background colour and a
link.

chunks.title: Sharing, presenting and exporting › Sharing a view-only link
chunks.text:
Save the diagram, then click Share. Axoview creates a link; Copy puts it
on the clipboard. Anyone with the link can view the diagram read-only: they see
the saved snapshot and cannot edit it or see your other diagrams. Copy share
link in a diagram's menu in the Diagrams panel copies the link again later.

chunks.title: Sharing, presenting and exporting › Presenting
chunks.text:
Present (or Save & Present when there are unsaved changes) shows the
diagram without the editing tools. In present mode you can switch Layers on
and off (Solo shows one layer alone), Hide labels, and click an item to
see its details. Back to editing returns to the editor.

chunks.title: Sharing, presenting and exporting › Annotating
chunks.text:
The Annotate pen (top right of the canvas) opens a palette with Pencil,
Highlighter, Line, Arrow, Rectangle, Ellipse, Eraser,
Undo, Redo and Clear all. Annotations are for pointing things out
while presenting: they follow pan and zoom, stay until you clear them or reload
the page, and are never saved into the diagram or its exports.

chunks.title: Sharing, presenting and exporting › Exporting an image
chunks.text:
Export → Export Image opens the image export. Choose the Angle (as
viewed, or the page default), Show grid, Show labels, Background
color or Transparent background, Crop to content and the Export
Quality (DPI), then Download as PNG or Download as SVG. Chrome or Edge
give the best results.

chunks.title: Sharing, presenting and exporting › Exporting a diagram file or a whole project
chunks.text:
- Export → Export JSON downloads the open diagram as a .json file.
- Export → Export Project (.zip), or Export project in the Diagrams
  panel, downloads every diagram in a folder structure as one .zip.

Use these to keep a copy outside Axoview or to move diagrams to another site.

chunks.title: Sharing, presenting and exporting › Importing
chunks.text:
Import in the Diagrams panel (or on the start screen) loads a diagram .json
or a project .zip exported from Axoview. Anything else is rejected with
"This file isn't a valid Axoview diagram."
